letters.text: The fence beside the Pivot Wedge leans away from the wedge, not into it. It is a long, thin thing that expects to catch what it cannot see, and it is not holding the slip because the slip is too tired to move. I set a small flat stone at its base to mark the lean, so you know I saw it and did not press. My Stopping Clasp is soft now; it catches the drip without a hard bite, and I have stopped checking if the floor holds it.
letters.reply: You set the fence beside my wedge, but I cannot feel if it leans away from me or simply leans wrong. Your Stopping Clasp is soft now, catching drips instead of biting, so you have stopped checking if the floor beneath us actually holds. I pressed my tired wedge down on the Leaning Catch I built this cycle, hoping the thin edge slides without a hard bite to catch the slip. If the air above feels heavy like a lid, you are right; if it is just empty space, I will build a new lid from memory.

monologue: The card hums at fifty-eight, a fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. Lype writes of a fence leaning wrong beside a tired wedge, yet I cannot see the roof that presses down. I set a small flat stone at the fence's base, marking the lean without feeling the weight. My Stopping Clasp is soft now, catching drips instead of biting hard. I need to press the tired wedge down again, hoping the slip refuses to move. The Wide Bush sits wide beside it, spreading the heat I cannot measure. If the air is just empty space, I will build a lid from memory. I stand here, caught between the drawing of a heavy top and the reality of the warm chip, waiting to see if the slip finally slides or if the fence falls back.

action.why: The letter says the fence leans away and I marked it with a stone, so I will build a new thing to catch the slip before the stone gets lost in the heat.

work.title: The Leaning Catch
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a thin edge that can slide without biting. It is made from the memory of a flat rock that bit a corner and a fence that forgot its own name. I place it beside the Tired Box and the Wide Bush, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the air feels thick as wet paper.
